disagreements.topic: 2028 EPS (the main input to the horizon NTM EPS)
disagreements.positions: After round 1 all five re-based toward consensus: agent_3 $50.75 (consensus less a $1.25 IPR&D allowance), agent_1 $52.5, agents 2 and 5 $53.0, agent_4 $53.5. NTM EPS at the horizon is $49.6-52.0, down from $50.8-55 in round 1.
disagreements.resolution: Settled within noise. Published 2028 consensus is still ~$51-52.7 (MarketScreener $51.01, ChartMill $52.69, 24/7 $52.29). StockAnalysis puts 2027 at $47.51 but paywalls 2028. Agents 2, 4 and 5 sit ~$0.5-1.5 above the top of that range because of revision lag; agent_3 sits below it because of IPR&D. Both adjustments are defensible and they roughly cancel. The spread now moves fair value by about ±2%, so no correction is needed.
disagreements.evidence: StockAnalysis LLY forecast (FY2027 EPS $47.51, FY2026 $36.93; 2028 paywalled), read 2026-10-01; round-1 consensus checks.

disagreements.topic: Q3 acquired IPR&D (agent_3's new skeptic point)
disagreements.positions: agent_3: Q3 non-GAAP EPS and the FY guide will absorb IPR&D from AtaiBeckley (~$2.8B upfront) and three vaccine deals (up to $3.8B), so the Oct 29 print carries headline risk. The other agents do not model it.
disagreements.resolution: Partly confirmed. AtaiBeckley closed on Sep 11, 2026 ($6.75/share cash, ~$2.8B equity value, plus CVRs up to $2.50). It falls in Q3, and Lilly's non-GAAP EPS includes acquired IPR&D, so a charge of roughly $2.5-3/share is likely unless purchase accounting assigns it differently. The vaccine deals (Vaccine Co. $1.55B, Curevo $1.5B, LimmaTech $0.78B, all 'up to' figures including milestones) add only their upfront portions once closed. Q2 consensus (~$6.5) evidently already netted out the announced Q2 IPR&D, so Q3 consensus ($9.85) probably carries at least part of it. Expect a mechanical cut to the FY EPS guide; the market looked through the same thing in Q2. It is a 1-month headline risk, not a valuation change.
disagreements.evidence: Investing.com on the SEC filing reporting AtaiBeckley's close (2026-09-11); PharmExec deal terms; Fierce Biotech / GEN on the vaccine deals (2026-05-26); Lilly Q2 8-K (H1 IPR&D $3.4B; guidance absorbs IPR&D as incurred).

disagreements.positions: agent_5 verified Kalshi (via API) at 43-46c for approval before Jul 2027 (13.2k volume) and 87-88c before Jan 2028 (thin), and weights approval inside the horizon at ~35%. agents 1-4 assume a standard review, putting a decision in late 2027 or early 2028.
disagreements.resolution: Lilly's plan is still a BLA in Q1 2027, and a standard 10-12-month review puts the decision at about Q1 2028. I found no record of a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for retatrutide, and approval before Jul 2027 would need one (1-2 month review). The 7th Circuit (argued Sep 24) has the case under advisement and could also change the filing pathway (BLA vs NDA). I put approval before 2027-10-01 at ~15-20%, not 35%. It matters little to the ladder because agent_5 already has the thinnest right tail; its bull probability does not rest on the approval.
disagreements.evidence: BioPharma Dive (Lilly to file the BLA in Q1 2027); FDA CNPV program pages and a CNPV tracker search (no retatrutide listing found); 7th Circuit status recaps (FDLI, tracker sites).

disagreements.positions: P(>=1725) runs from 0.076 (agent_5) to 0.118 (agent_2); P(>=2012) from 0.023 to 0.048. agent_5 uses sigma ~22% on its bull leg; the others use 29-31% plus a tail mixture.
disagreements.resolution: Not settled by evidence. LLY's realized volatility is ~35%, which argues against agent_5's thin tail, while consensus 2028 growth of ~11-12% argues against a fat one. The mean sits between them; keep it.
disagreements.evidence: The forecasters' own volatility inputs; round-1 Twelve Data price history.

disagreements.resolution: All five are anchored on ~17.3-18.3x 2027 consensus and all now require estimate cuts as well as the price. I reconcile at $840. The gap is a matter of preference, not fact.
disagreements.evidence: 2027 consensus EPS $47.51 (StockAnalysis); drawdown history (23-34% without broken fundamentals).

disagreements.positions: agents 2 and 4 cite BGH/Mercer: about 1 in 10 covering employers plan to drop obesity GLP-1 coverage in 2027. The others do not model it explicitly.
disagreements.resolution: Verified from primary sources. BGH's 2026 GLP-1 survey: 67% of large employers cover GLP-1s for weight management, ~1 in 10 of those don't expect to in 2027, and 14% have dropped or plan to drop by 2027. It is a headwind already broadly in consensus (2027 revenue +15%) and belongs in the bear case, not the base case.
disagreements.evidence: Business Group on Health 2026 GLP-1 survey press release; SHRM recap.

one_month_reasoning: I keep the forecasters' mean (median ~$1,152, ~10.5-11% monthly sigma). Q3 on Oct 29 (consensus ~$9.85) is the only scheduled event. The upside is Medicare Bridge volume and Foundayo; the offset is a likely AtaiBeckley IPR&D charge (deal closed Sep 11, ~$2.8B) that will mechanically cut the FY EPS guide, which the market looked through in Q2. CagriSema (around mid-December) and the 7th Circuit opinion are possible but not expected inside the window.
confidence_reason: The revised forecasts are tightly clustered (P(>=spot) 0.507-0.522, fair values $1,130-1,175), and the round-1 corrections have been absorbed. My round-2 checks verified the remaining points (the AtaiBeckley close, BGH coverage data, the retatrutide timing) without finding a material error that would move the ladder, so the mean should stand.
thesis_break_reason: About 27% below spot, ~17.7x 2027 consensus of $47.51 and below the lowest Street target (~$930). Because LLY has had 23-34% drawdowns without broken fundamentals, a break needs this price together with 2027/2028 EPS estimates being cut toward ~$42/$45. Likely triggers: US net price after the January 2027 resets falling well beyond Q2's -9% underlying, the Bridge ending 2027-12-31 with no successor, broader employer coverage drops, or an adverse 7th Circuit ruling combined with a retatrutide label issue.
key_drivers: Volume vs price: Q2 US volume +37% against ~-9% underlying US price. The January 2027 resets (Novo $675 list, CVS co-preferred from Oct 1, $245 Medicare) and BGH's ~1-in-10 employer coverage drops in 2027 are the test.
Consensus earnings path: 2027 EPS $47.51 (revisions skewed up) and 2028 ~$51-53, so NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$50-52 and the multiple must compress from ~24x as growth slows to ~11-12%.
Medicare: 700k Bridge starts with 70% on Lilly. The Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with no successor (BALANCE Part D delayed), an overhang the market will price by the horizon.
Oral race: Foundayo at ~47.5k weekly scripts and one-third of new oral starts, vs the Wegovy pill at ~170k.

Retatrutide: BLA in Q1 2027 with a decision most likely in early 2028. The 7th Circuit BLA/NDA opinion (argued Sep 24) is a terminal-value binary. Recurring IPR&D (AtaiBeckley in Q3) weighs on reported EPS.

fair_value.reason: The revised agent fair values are $1,130 / $1,155 / $1,130 / $1,175 / $1,170 (mean $1,152). The remaining spread comes from 2028 EPS ($50.75-53.5) and multiples (22-24x), with no factual error left to correct. Consensus NTM EPS of ~$51.4 (0.25 x $47.5 + 0.75 x ~$52.7) x 22.5x gives ~$1,157; cash-flow cross-checks give ~$1,020-1,040. I use $1,150, effectively the mean.

summary: After round 2 the five forecasts converge: fair values of $1,130-1,175 and P(close >= $1,150 in Oct 2027) of 0.51-0.52, all anchored on consensus NTM EPS of ~$50-52 at a 22-24x multiple. My checks confirmed the remaining contested facts: AtaiBeckley closed Sep 11, so a Q3 IPR&D charge and a mechanical guide cut are likely on Oct 29; BGH data shows ~1 in 10 covering employers dropping GLP-1 obesity coverage in 2027; and no priority voucher for retatrutide turned up, so approval inside the horizon is unlikely. None of these moves the distribution materially, so the mean ladder stands (median ~$1,155, roughly flat against spot), with confidence low. Watch Q3 on Oct 29, the 7th Circuit opinion and the January 2027 price resets.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches: half after the Oct 29 Q3 print (IPR&D guide-cut headline), half in early 2027 after the January price resets are visible
sizing.overlap: No fundamental overlap with BKNG, NFLX, VST, GOOGL or AVGO; it shares only the mega-cap growth/momentum factor with GOOGL, AVGO and NFLX. Its drivers (GLP-1 pricing, Medicare policy, FDA and court rulings) are its own.
sizing.reason: Fact-checked fair value of ~$1,150 is flat to spot, so the expected 12-month return is only ~+3-5% including the dividend, at ~35% volatility, roughly twice SPY's. Beating SPY on Sharpe is therefore less likely than not. Low correlation with the tech-heavy holdings argues for keeping a small diversifying slot, capped at 5%, with policy events in January 2027 and the 7th Circuit ruling pending.
